subject: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Ops <cloudops@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment

Team / Sarah —

We are targeting the private deployment go-live for ACME tonight (18:00 PDT). This thread is the formal acceptance checkpoint and the evacuation/escape-hatch plan we will use if any hard-fail criteria are tripped during the first 2 hours of live traffic. Please review the runbook and confirm ownership of the items below by EOD.

Attachments: runbook-v1.pdf, firewall_rules_snapshot.txt, smoke-results-template.csv

Immediate asks:
- Aditya: confirm KV cache warm pass and kube node probes (see runbook §2.1).
- Jonas: confirm ops-bridge number and who will be on call for the canary window.
- Monica: coordinate with ACME on scheduled client traffic window and confirm they have DNS TTL change plan.
- Irene: confirm final IAM policy snapshot and KMS key binding.
- Sarah: can your team run the planned failover test at 17:30 and confirm the expected traffic drain time?

Escalation criteria (from runbook §4):
- API p95 latency > 1.2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes OR
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% sustained for 3 minutes OR
- KV cache miss storm causing >20% tail latency regression

Escape hatch (high-level):
1) Pause incoming traffic at the edge and route to hosted fallback pool (approx 6-8 minute cut).
2) If we cannot restore within 20 minutes, trigger rollback to previous VM image and reintroduce traffic behind a throttled gate.

Please reply with confirmations inline. I'll consolidate and publish the final checkpoint at 15:30.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0128

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment

Marissa — quick confirmations and technical notes inline.

- KV cache warm: will run warmup script starting 16:00 PDT. Expect ~12 minutes to reach target hit-rate on primary shard. I attached kv_cache_warm.log from the last rehearsal.
- Node probes: readiness/read timeout set to 10s; liveness at 30s. Confirmed with infra (no change from staging).
- Firewall rules snapshot: ran diff against previous snapshot; there are two new egress ports to 10.2.0.0/16 for telemetry (allowed). I recommend we keep the temporary allow with a 24h TTL; otherwise we need a patch window.

Escape hatch notes:
- Routing to hosted fallback uses VIP switch at the edge; estimated client-visible disruption: ~6 minutes (DNS + LB drain). We validated this in canary on 2028-04-10.
- If KV miss storm detected, we will enable prefix caching (fast path) and throttle write-heavy streams; this is documented in runbook §4.2.

Attachments: kv_cache_warm.log

Action: I will kick warmup at 16:00 and report completion to this thread.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment

Marissa / team — thanks for the plan. A few clarifications from ACME side: 

- We can run the targeted failover at 17:30 but our downstream batch jobs run at 19:00 — please ensure any prolonged disruption does not overlap that window.
- Our DNS TTL for the primary edge is 45s; we can temporarily reduce to 30s at 17:45 if needed but prefer to avoid changes before 18:00.
- We will have two engineers on the bridge (Sarah + Miguel) and will run the failover test once Aditya confirms warmup.

One ask: can you list the exact rollback image tag you would use in the escape hatch? We want to pre-approve and keep a copy in our registry.

—Sarah Jensen
Sr. Manager, Cloud Operations | Acme Corp
sarah.jensen@acme.com | +1 (415) 555-2299

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment

Thanks — confirm items and ops bridge details: 

- Ops bridge: +1 (844) 700-REDW (PIN 4281). On-call rotation: Jonas (canary window), Monica (rollback support), Irene (security/IAM).
- Rollback image tag: redwood-prod-acme:v20280314-stable. We will stage a copy to ACME registry under acme/redwood-backed/v20280314-stable and share the pull token.
- Canary window: 18:00–18:20 PDT. We will start with 1% traffic, then 10% at 18:05, 50% at 18:10, full at 18:15 if no red flags.

Quoted from Sarah's note: "please ensure any prolonged disruption does not overlap our downstream batch jobs at 19:00" — noted; we'll enforce a hard stop at 18:50 for any remediation that might impact batch.

Action items (owners):
- Aditya: KV warm at 16:00 (report to thread).
- Monica: coordinate DNS TTL reduction fallback and ACME contact list.
- Irene: upload final IAM policy snapshot to drive link.
- Marissa: publish acceptance checkpoint and confirm final go/no-go at 15:30.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance checkpoint: ops-bridge & evacuation plan for ACME private deployment — FINAL CHECKPOINT

All — thank you for the fast responses. Consolidated status below: 

- KV warm: scheduled 16:00 (Aditya).
- Ops bridge: confirmed (Jonas/Monica/Irene) — dial-in + bridge will be stood up at 17:45.
- Rollback image: redwood-prod-acme:v20280314-stable (staged to ACME registry). ACME to confirm pull token receipt.
- ACME failover test: scheduled 17:30; ACME to confirm result in this thread.
- Hard stop: 18:50 for any changes that might touch downstream batch jobs at 19:00.

I am publishing this as the formal acceptance checkpoint. If there are no objections, we will proceed with the planned go-live and follow the canary cadence. If any of the escalation criteria are met during the window, we will enact the escape hatch and inform ACME and leadership immediately.

Final ask: ACME, please reply after the 17:30 failover test with a single-line pass/fail and any observed failover time.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Head of Deployments, Redwood Inference
